segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: What do you check when one hearth sector warms but cooling flow appears normal?

segments.speaker: operator
segments.text: When one hearth sector warms but cooling flow appears normal, I watch for persistence across taps and slower cooling after a tap.

segments.speaker: operator
segments.text: I compare the sector with neighboring shell thermocouples and check cooling-water inlet and outlet temperature and recent flow history, not only the current flow.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: How do you tell a failing thermocouple from real lining degradation?

segments.speaker: operator
segments.text: A single reading can mislead; corroboration lowers the chance of reacting to an instrument fault.

segments.speaker: operator
segments.text: I validate sensor health and recent calibration, and request a cooling-circuit inspection and ultrasound measurement when the signals agree.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: What should a new operator never change without engineering approval?

segments.speaker: operator
segments.text: A new operator must never bypass alarms or change furnace or cooling controls without engineering approval.
